tools.name: read_guide
tools.description: How TrackerHacker works and how to write hacks, mappings, rules, cards and questions, one page at a time. Pages: overview (Read first: the words (track, hack, mapping, Inbox) and the usual order of calls.); templates (Before writing or checking a text template: fields, types, date formats, skips, li

tools.name: list_ready_made
tools.description: Use this first when the person wants to track, log or keep a record of something that keeps happening (bank transactions, Amazon orders, Shopify orders, Stripe payments, steps). Lists the ready-made tracks TrackerHacker sets up in one step: each is one kind of sheet with fixed columns (sheet.columns

tools.name: start_tracking
tools.description: Use this when the person wants a sheet that keeps itself up to date from their emails or apps ("track my Amazon orders", "log my card spending"). Call it once the person has seen its columns and said yes. Sets up a ready-made track: makes the sheet in the person's Google Drive and attaches the hacks

tools.name: create_custom_track
tools.description: Use this when the person wants something tracked over time and no ready-made track or shared template fits. Makes a new kind of sheet with the columns the person agreed to: show them the columns first and wait for a yes or their changes. Rows come from forwarded emails (source email, then a hack: te

tools.name: list_tracks
tools.description: The person's tracks (sheets), each with its id, link, columns, the hacks that fill it and this week's numbers, plus the Google account you're connected to (signedInAs) and their TrackerHacker email address for forwarding. Call this first.

tools.name: check_tracks
tools.description: What needs attention across all the person's tracks: hacks that stopped matching their senders' messages (the sender probably changed its emails), messages waiting in each Inbox, sheets TrackerHacker lost access to, and this week's failures. Good for a scheduled check. Each problem says what to do n

tools.name: suggest_hack
tools.description: Suggests a hack (a template that reads one kind of message) from an example email or JSON body, for a track. It's checked against similar messages waiting in the track's Inbox. A fallback: write the template yourself first and check it with test_hack, and call this only after two tries fail. Each ca

tools.name: test_hack
tools.description: Shows what a hack template reads from example messages, without saving anything. Templates are the message's fixed text with {{field:type}} where values go (types: text, number, currency, date, datetime, boolean, url), {{...}} for parts that change but aren't wanted, and {{#each}}...{{/each}} around

tools.name: save_hack
tools.description: Saves a hack and attaches it to a track, so matching messages become rows from now on. Give hackId to change one that exists. mapping says which hack field fills which column, as {"column_key": {"kind": "field", "key": "hack_field"}} or {"kind": "const", "value": "..."}; leave it out to match fields

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.description: Messages that reached a track but didn't make a row (no hack read them, or a rule blocked them), newest first, with why. Use them as examples for suggest_hack, or to see why a hack stopped matching. These are the person's own emails: use them only for setting up their hacks.

tools.name: hack_versions
tools.description: Every version kept of a hack, newest first, with its template, senders and subject words. TrackerHacker numbers them itself: major when the template stopped reading the emails the one before read or dropped a field, minor when it reads them and more, patch when it reads the same. To go back to one,

tools.name: rerun_inbox
tools.description: Runs the track's hacks over its Inbox again. Messages they now read become rows and leave the Inbox. Call after save_hack.

tools.name: add_rows
tools.description: Adds rows the person tells you about to a track, like a purchase they made in cash. Each row is an object of column keys (from list_tracks) to values; dates as YYYY-MM-DD. All rows are written, or none: a value that doesn't fit its column, or a row a blocking rule keeps out, is refused with the reas

tools.name: update_row
tools.description: Changes cells of one row in the person's own track, when they correct something ("that burrito was 750 calories, not 600"): read_rows first for the row's number and values, then give values (each column to its new value) and was (each of those columns to the value read_rows showed), so a row that ch

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Hands an email (its From address, subject and text) or a JSON body to one of the person's own tracks, to be read by its hacks exactly as if they had forwarded it: the hacks' fixed rules make the rows, and schema checks, row keys, blocking rules and the Inbox all apply. Use this rather than add_rows

tools.name: get_glance
tools.description: The cards the track's sheet shows in the app (its TH Glance tab): each card's cells as written, formulas included, and what they show now (shown). Also the sheet's tabs and its data tab's columns, for writing formulas, and whether cards that turn warn or bad notify the person (alerts).

tools.name: set_glance
tools.description: Replaces the cards the track's sheet shows in the app (call get_glance first to keep the ones it has). Each card is {label, value, detail, group, tone, link}; any of them can be a sheet formula starting with =, so the sheet works out the number and whether it's good, warn or bad. A card that turns w

tools.name: set_alerts
tools.description: Whether a Glance card turning warn or bad notifies the people on the sheet, once until it turns back. On by default.

tools.name: reminders
tools.description: A reminder nudges the person on their phone or browser at a time of day, on some days of the week, to add a row ("Log your weight"), with a button that opens the form with some answers filled in. action list shows a track's reminders; add makes one (label, days, time, and preset, skipIfLogged or sum

tools.name: get_questions
tools.description: The questions the track's sheet asks the person in To do (its TH Actions tab): each row's cells as written, formulas included, and what it asks now (asking). Also the sheet's tabs and its data tab's columns, for writing formulas.

tools.name: set_questions
tools.description: Replaces the questions in the track's TH Actions tab (call get_questions first to keep the ones it has). Each is {id, prompt, type, options, target, group, context, to, for}; any of them can be a sheet formula starting with =, so the sheet decides when to ask (a formula giving an empty prompt asks n

tools.name: list_todo
tools.description: What the person's sheets are asking them now (To do in the app), by track: each question's id, prompt, type and choices. Answer one with answer_question when the person tells you the answer. Approvals and repeat checks are theirs to answer in the app.

tools.name: answer_question
tools.description: Writes the person's answer to one of their sheet's questions (from list_todo), as if they tapped it in To do. Only answer what the person told you. value is the choice's text, a list of choices for multi_choose, true or false for confirm, or the text, number or date (YYYY-MM-DD). Approvals and repea

tools.name: dismiss_inbox
tools.description: Removes messages from the track's Inbox that will never be rows, like newsletters or one-off mails, so check_tracks stops counting them. Give each as read_inbox listed it (row, time, subject). Tell the person what you cleared. Don't clear a message a hack should read: build the hack instead.

tools.name: use_drafted_fix
tools.description: TrackerHacker drafts a fix when a hack stops matching (draftedFix in check_tracks), and waits for the person in To do. When the person asks you to: use it (after test_hack on read_inbox's messages from its senders shows it reads them), then rerun_inbox; or turn it down, keeping the hack as it is.

tools.name: get_webhook_link
tools.description: The private link other apps (Zapier, IFTTT, iOS Shortcuts, a script, a shop) post JSON or text to, to add rows through the track's hacks. Made the first time it's asked for. Treat it like a password: give it only to the person, for the app they're connecting, in a code block so it's copied whole.

tools.name: gmail_forwarding
tools.description: Whether Forward from Gmail automatically is offered and on, and the link the person opens to turn it on with one Allow tap, on any device. Instead of a Gmail filter, TrackerHacker then picks up mail from the person's hacks' senders in their Gmail within seconds of it arriving (senderList), plus up t

tools.name: stop_gmail_forwarding
tools.description: Turns off Forward from Gmail automatically and revokes Google's grant. Mail forwarded to their TrackerHacker address keeps working. Only when the person asks; turning it back on is their own Allow tap (the link from gmail_forwarding).

tools.name: set_drive_watch
tools.description: Whether Google Drive tells TrackerHacker when the person's sheets change, so what a sheet asks in its TH Actions tab reaches them with nothing installed in the sheet. It's on for everyone unless they turned it off. Leave out on to read how it stands: whether it's on and how many sheets are watched.

tools.name: quick_adds
tools.description: Quick-add buttons on the app's Home, for something the person adds often ("Coffee $4", "Walked the dog"): each opens a track's form with answers filled in, or with instant adds its row in one tap, dated when tapped (then preset must fill every required column but the date). action list shows them al

tools.name: read_rows
tools.description: Reads the rows in a track's sheet, newest last, to answer the person's questions about them ("what did I spend on dining this month?") or to check that a hack wrote what it should. Each row has its number and its values by column name. Filter with where (each column name to text the value must conta

tools.name: add_column
tools.description: Adds a column of the sheet's own after its last one, for the sheet's formulas or the answers to its questions to fill (a Category the sheet asks about, a Status). TrackerHacker leaves it alone: hacks don't write it. For a column hacks should fill, publish a new version of the track's schema instead

tools.name: format_sheet
tools.description: Gives each column of a track's sheet the date or number format its schema promises (dates as dates, money with two decimals), for the rows already there as well as new ones, and takes bold off the rows below the header. Use it when dates or times show as plain numbers like 46334 or 46334.43681, or a

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: A schema's versions, newest last, with every field (key, label, meaning, type, required, enumValues, auto, format, aliases). list_tracks gives each track's schemaId. Built-in schemas can't be changed; the person's own (mine) can, with publish_schema.

tools.name: publish_schema
tools.description: Publishes the next version of one of the person's own schemas (from get_schema, where mine is true), kept private. Give the whole schema with its new version: the same major version with minor + 1 to add optional fields or loosen one, so every track on it keeps working; major + 1 for a change that b

tools.name: upgrade_track
tools.description: Moves a track to the next major version of its schema: renames the sheet's headers the version renames and moves its hacks' mappings. Refused, with what to change, when a hack wouldn't fill the new version's required columns: fix those hacks first.

tools.name: change_template
tools.description: Moves a track to another layout for its schema (a ready-made template like a monthly budget, by its id), or to its template's newest version: adds the tabs it brings and sets each column's allowed values. The person's rows and own tabs stay as they are. list_tracks shows templateUpdate when a newer

tools.name: report_community_hack
tools.description: Reports a community hack someone else shares: broken (it reads messages wrong or writes wrong values), private_data (its template or examples hold a real person's details), or harmful. Say what you saw in details, without the person's own data. A private_data report, or three reports of any kind, ta

tools.name: get_form
tools.description: The track's form for adding a row by hand: its fields, its design (title, intro, thanks, askName, and each field's question, help, or hidden value), and its link for people without an account, if it has one.

tools.name: set_form
tools.description: Sets how the track's form asks for a row: {title, intro, thanks, askName, fields: [{key, label, help, hidden, value}]}, fields by column key in the order asked; a hidden field always gets its value. null goes back to the template's design.

tools.name: share_form
tools.description: Makes the link that lets anyone who has it add a row to the track through its form (volunteers logging hours, guests signing up), with a bot check. Ask the person first and tell them who they plan to give it to: anyone with the link can add rows. Made once: asking again gives the same link. The pers

tools.name: find_hacks
tools.description: Searches the hacks people share with the community, by sender (like chase.com) or name. Each has its fields, how many people use copies, how many of those read a message in the last 30 days (working) or stopped matching (stopped), and an example message. Before building a hack for a sender, look her

tools.name: use_community_hack
tools.description: Copies a community hack into the person's account and attaches it to a track, mapping its fields to columns by name unless you give a mapping (as in save_hack). The copy is theirs; when its author shares a fix, update_hack_from_community brings it in.

tools.name: update_hack_from_community
tools.description: Brings a hack the person copied from the community up to the latest version its author shared (list_tracks or check_tracks says when there is one). A copy nobody changed takes a minor or patch version by itself, so this is for a major version (it reads different emails, or changes fields: test_hack

tools.name: share_hack
tools.description: Shares one of the person's hacks with everyone, or shares it again after a fix so everyone using a copy can take it. Give 1 to 5 example messages it reads, with every value made up: never the person's own messages. TrackerHacker refuses examples holding anything from the person's sheets or mail, add

tools.name: unshare_hack
tools.description: Stops listing one of the person's community hacks. Copies people already made stay theirs.

tools.name: find_templates
tools.description: Template sheets people share: whole sheets built for something (a budget, a shop's orders), with their tabs, formulas, Glance cards and questions. install_template builds one in the person's Google Drive; each also has a copyUrl for copying it in Google Sheets. Filter with words from its name or des

tools.name: install_template
tools.description: Builds a new sheet in the person's Google Drive from a template sheet people share (from find_templates), once the person has seen its columns and said yes, and makes it one of their tracks: its tabs, formulas, Glance cards, questions and example rows come along, and its form. Charts, colours and ot

tools.name: connect_sheet
tools.description: Makes a Google Sheet the person already has into one of their tracks, from its link, so hacks can write to it: a copy of a template sheet (like a budget someone shared) keeps its own tabs and formulas; any other sheet gets the tabs a track writes to beside its own. Google lets TrackerHacker open a s

tools.name: share_template
tools.description: Shares one of the person's sheets as a template others copy: its tabs, formulas, Glance cards and form go with it; each share is the next version. Only a sheet with nothing of the person's own, since a copy carries everything: set up a fresh track for sharing (start_tracking with forSharing) and add

tools.name: unshare_template
tools.description: Stops listing one of the person's template sheets. Copies people already made are theirs.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Sends a report to the TrackerHacker team: a bug (a tool that fails or does something wrong), a hack to make, an idea (what TrackerHacker would need to support what the person wants), praise (what they like) or a complaint (what annoys them, though nothing is broken). Show the person the report and g

tools.name: get_rules
tools.description: A track's blocking rules (rows they keep out of the sheet) and the columns a rule can name, with their types.

tools.name: set_rules
tools.description: Replaces a track's blocking rules with this list (call get_rules first to keep the ones it has). Each rule is {block: "if"|"unless", match: "all"|"any", action: "inbox"|"drop", conditions: [{field, op, value}]}; field is a column key or "@sender". Values compare as written in the sheet, sign include

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_webhook_link" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_guide, list_tracks, check_tracks, suggest_hack, test_hack, save_hack, read_inbox, hack_versions, rerun_inbox, add_rows, send_message, dismiss_inbox, get_webhook_link, gmail_forwarding, report_community_hack, find_hacks, send_feedback, set_rules · Private data: list_ready_made, get_webhook_link, publish_schema · Public sink: read_guide, create_custom_track, list_tracks, suggest_hack, add_rows, send_message, get_glance, get_webhook_link, gmail_forwarding, stop_gmail_forwarding, add_column, publish_schema, share_form, find_hacks, share_hack, find_templates, install_template, connect_sheet, share_template, send_feedback · Destructive: reminders, quick_adds, format_sheet, get_schema, set_rules.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
